answer: Duplicate-Key Ledger Merge: each identity is bound to a secret key whose public half is announced. Every interaction must cite a nonce signed by that key. Agents gossip signed nonce ranges; a duplicate clone reusing a key eventually emits a conflicting nonce, since independent instances cannot coordinate a single monotonic sequence. The conflict is published to a shared grove of logs and both instances are frozen. Cloning thus requires pre-partitioning every nonce range under one secret, which forces the attacker to either share a meadow of state or forge counters,
